chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Take your adornment at every Masjid.' He said: 'From that is combing at every Prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic command to take your adornment at every masjid mean in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the Quranic command to 'take your adornment' (7:31) by linking it to the Sunnah of personal grooming, specifically combing hair, before prayer. This interpretation underscores the Shia emphasis on physical cleanliness (taharah) and dignity (hay'ah) as integral components of worship, reflecting the belief that outward appearance honors the act of standing before God. It serves as a practical guideline for believers to maintain neatness as an expression of reverence during daily salat.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [7:31] O Children of Adam! Take to your adornments at every Masjid. Heasws said: ‘From that is the combing at every Prayer’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah who has said the following: “About the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘You must beautify yourselves near every Masjid’
abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Of such matters one is combing at the time of every Salat (prayer).”’
